net_new_papers.track: Track 24: Behavioral Finance Quant Signals: Limited Attention, Salience, Anchoring, Disposition Effect & Investor Sentiment
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Exploits FAS 123-R's shift of option compensation expense from footnotes to the income statement; even with unchanged fundamentals, moving salient costs onto the main statement triggers earnings misses, downgrades, and valuation declines due to investor inattention to footnote details.

net_new_papers.title: News Diffusion in Social Networks and Stock Market Reactions
net_new_papers.authors: David Hirshleifer, Lin Peng & Qiguang Wang
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: Behavioral Finance Quant Signals: Limited Attention, Salience, Anchoring, Disposition Effect & Investor Sentiment
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Proposes the "social churning hypothesis": firms in high social-network centrality counties experience stronger immediate earnings-day price, volatility, and volume reactions, followed by weaker post-earnings announcement drift (PEAD) and faster volatility decay, but persistently elevated turnover.

net_new_papers.title: Salience theory and stock returns: The role of reference-dependent preferences
net_new_papers.authors: Jihoon Goh, Suk-Joon Byun & Donghoon Kim
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: Behavioral Finance Quant Signals: Limited Attention, Salience, Anchoring, Disposition Effect & Investor Sentiment
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Interacts salience theory with capital gains overhang (CGO): the salience effect is concentrated among stocks in prior capital loss regions (where loss-domain risk-seeking amplifies preference for salient upsides) and is muted or reversed in gain regions.

net_new_papers.title: The change in salience and the cross-section of stock returns: Empirical evidence from China A-shares
net_new_papers.authors: Manqing Zhang, Yao Ma, Baochen Yang & Ying Fan
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: Behavioral Finance Quant Signals: Limited Attention, Salience, Anchoring, Disposition Effect & Investor Sentiment
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Introduces the *change in salience* (CS) signal rather than static ST levels: both retail and institutional investors extrapolate prominent rising return trends, causing positive-CS stocks to become overpriced and earn significantly lower subsequent returns.

net_new_papers.title: Corporate insiders' exploitation of investors' anchoring bias at the 52-week high and low
net_new_papers.authors: Meziane Lasfer & Xiaoke Ye
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: Behavioral Finance Quant Signals: Limited Attention, Salience, Anchoring, Disposition Effect & Investor Sentiment
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Shows corporate insiders (Form 4) exploit outside investors' anchoring at 52-week highs/lows: insider purchases near 52-week highs and insider sales near 52-week lows carry substantially stronger abnormal return predictability than unconditional insider trades.

net_new_papers.title: At the Top of the Mind: Peak Prices and the Disposition Effect
net_new_papers.authors: Edika Quispe-Torreblanca, David Hume, John Gathergood, George Loewenstein & Neil Stewart
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: Behavioral Finance Quant Signals: Limited Attention, Salience, Anchoring, Disposition Effect & Investor Sentiment
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Demonstrates that the peak price achieved *during an investor's holding period* (post-purchase peak) acts as an independent, overlapping salient reference point alongside purchase price, driving selling reluctance even when the position is nominally in the green.

net_new_papers.title: The Law of Small Numbers in Financial Markets: Theory and Evidence
net_new_papers.authors: Lawrence J. Jin & Cameron Peng
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: Behavioral Finance Quant Signals: Limited Attention, Salience, Anchoring, Disposition Effect & Investor Sentiment
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Unifies the disposition effect, doubling-down in buying, and return extrapolation under the Law of Small Numbers (LSN): LSN beliefs generate short-term contrarianism/momentum alongside long-term reversals and decompose the V-shaped selling propensity across investor types.

net_new_papers.title: Dynamic Trading with Realization Utility
net_new_papers.authors: Min Dai, Cong Qin & Neng Wang
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: Behavioral Finance Quant Signals: Limited Attention, Salience, Anchoring, Disposition Effect & Investor Sentiment
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Solves a dynamic portfolio model with realization utility, downward price jumps, and account-level mental budgeting: leverage amplifies the disposition effect via reluctance to realize losses, whereas cash savings and jumps enable voluntary deep-loss liquidation.

net_new_papers.title: Does social media information affect individual investor disposition effect? Evidence from Xueqiu
net_new_papers.authors: Siliu Chen & Fei Ren
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: Behavioral Finance Quant Signals: Limited Attention, Salience, Anchoring, Disposition Effect & Investor Sentiment
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Combines Xueqiu social investment posts with actual individual trading records to show that exposure to *negative* social media information significantly attenuates the disposition effect, accelerating rational loss realization.

net_new_papers.title: Taming the bias zoo
net_new_papers.authors: Hongqi Liu, Cameron Peng, Wei A. Xiong & Wei Xiong
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: Behavioral Finance Quant Signals: Limited Attention, Salience, Anchoring, Disposition Effect & Investor Sentiment
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Integrates nationwide retail survey responses with actual brokerage turnover to resolve observational equivalence among behavioral biases: perceived information advantage and gambling preference dominate turnover regressions over other surveyed biases.

net_new_papers.title: Salience and return reversals: Evidence from China
net_new_papers.authors: Xiao Li & Xirou Yang
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: Behavioral Finance Quant Signals: Limited Attention, Salience, Anchoring, Disposition Effect & Investor Sentiment
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Proposes *deviation salience* (DS), measuring a stock's return deviation relative to industry peers: high-DS stocks exhibit strong short-term return reversals (with salience amplifying reactions to bad news more than good news) driven by attention-induced overreaction.

net_new_papers.title: 4/2 rough and smooth
net_new_papers.authors: Tingjin Yan, Jie Yin, Ling Wang & Hoi Ying Wong
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Rough Volatility, Fractional Brownian Motion, Hawkes Processes & Point-Process Order Flow Modeling
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Combines rough Heston (rough $1/2$) and smooth $3/2$ variance dynamics into a parsimonious 4/2 two-factor model with semi-closed-form SPX and VIX pricing, outperforming benchmarks in- and out-of-sample.

net_new_papers.title: VIX Term Structure in the Rough Heston Model via Markovian Approximation
net_new_papers.authors: Yue Kuen Kwok & Yifan Ye
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Rough Volatility, Fractional Brownian Motion, Hawkes Processes & Point-Process Order Flow Modeling
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Develops a Markovian approximation with analytical squared-VIX and gradient formulas for rough Heston, outperforming jump-diffusion Heston models on daily VIX term structures and spot volatility estimation.

net_new_papers.title: A general valuation framework for rough stochastic local volatility models and applications
net_new_papers.authors: Wensheng Yang, Jingtang Ma & Zhenyu Cui
net_new_papers.venue: *European Journal of Operational Research*, vol. 322(1), pp. 307–324
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Rough Volatility, Fractional Brownian Motion, Hawkes Processes & Point-Process Order Flow Modeling
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Introduces a perturbed stochastic local volatility (PSLV) semimartingale approximation and continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) algorithm for rough SLV models, achieving fast, convergent pricing for European, barrier, and American options.

net_new_papers.title: Moments in Rough Bergomi and Boundary Attainment in Rough Heston
net_new_papers.authors: Arthur Bourdon & Thibault Jeannin
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Rough Volatility, Fractional Brownian Motion, Hawkes Processes & Point-Process Order Flow Modeling
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Establishes the exact moment-explosion threshold $p_\rho = (1-\rho^2)^{-1}$ in fractional rough Bergomi and proves the rough Heston variance law has a positive atom at zero at every positive time regardless of Feller-type conditions.

net_new_papers.title: Efficient Option Pricing in the Rough Heston Model Using Weak Simulation Schemes
net_new_papers.authors: Christian Bayer & Simon Breneis
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Rough Volatility, Fractional Brownian Motion, Hawkes Processes & Point-Process Order Flow Modeling
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Constructs second-order weak simulation schemes for standard ($H>0$) and hyper-rough ($H>-1/2$) Heston via low-dimensional Markovian approximations, reducing computational complexity from quadratic $O(n^2)$ to linear $O(n)$.

net_new_papers.title: Multiscaling and rough volatility: An empirical investigation
net_new_papers.authors: Giuseppe Brandi & Tiziana Di Matteo
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Rough Volatility, Fractional Brownian Motion, Hawkes Processes & Point-Process Order Flow Modeling
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Tests whether rough Bergomi reproduces the empirical interplay between price multiscaling and volatility Hurst roughness, uncovering an opposite sign in real data that exposes structural limits of monofractal rough volatility.

net_new_papers.title: Rough-Heston Local-Volatility Model
net_new_papers.authors: Enrico Dall'Acqua, Riccardo Longoni & Andrea Pallavicini
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Rough Volatility, Fractional Brownian Motion, Hawkes Processes & Point-Process Order Flow Modeling
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Extends Markovian projection to rough Heston with local volatility leverage functions, enabling simultaneous calibration to exotic path-dependent payoffs and short-dated implied volatility skews.

net_new_papers.title: Option Pricing with Time-Changed Fractional Brownian Motion: A Fractional Variance Gamma Model
net_new_papers.authors: Robert Jarrow & Jayen Tan
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Rough Volatility, Fractional Brownian Motion, Hawkes Processes & Point-Process Order Flow Modeling
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Subordinates fractional Brownian motion with a gamma clock to construct a fractional Variance Gamma model that jointly captures long-range dependence, heavy tails, and skewness in option pricing.

net_new_papers.title: Fractional Brownian motion in option pricing and dynamic delta hedging: Experimental simulations
net_new_papers.authors: Tamirat Temesgen Dufera
net_new_papers.venue: *The North American Journal of Economics and Finance*, vol. 69(PB)
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Rough Volatility, Fractional Brownian Motion, Hawkes Processes & Point-Process Order Flow Modeling
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Evaluates option valuation and dynamic delta-hedging replication errors under fractional Brownian motion across Hurst regimes via Monte Carlo experimental simulations.

net_new_papers.title: Option pricing in the illiquid markets under the mixed fractional Brownian motion model
net_new_papers.authors: Pengcheng Ma, Mehran Taghipour & Carlo Cattani
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Rough Volatility, Fractional Brownian Motion, Hawkes Processes & Point-Process Order Flow Modeling
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Formulates a mixed fractional geometric Brownian motion model with jumps and supply-demand illiquidity feedback, deriving and solving the replicating PIDE via spectral collocation.

net_new_papers.title: The fractional volatility model and rough volatility
net_new_papers.authors: R. Vilela Mendes
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Rough Volatility, Fractional Brownian Motion, Hawkes Processes & Point-Process Order Flow Modeling
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Reconciles long-memory fractional volatility models ($H > 0.5$) with apparent high-frequency roughness, examining no-arbitrage, leverage effects, and market completeness.

net_new_papers.title: Price modelling under generalized fractional Brownian motion
net_new_papers.authors: Axel A. Araneda
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Rough Volatility, Fractional Brownian Motion, Hawkes Processes & Point-Process Order Flow Modeling
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Develops generalized fractional Brownian motion price dynamics for derivative valuation, accommodating flexible non-stationary scaling and memory kernels beyond standard fBm.

net_new_papers.title: Convergence of Heavy-Tailed Hawkes Processes and the Microstructure of Rough Volatility
net_new_papers.authors: Ulrich Horst, Wei Xu & Rouyi Zhang
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Rough Volatility, Fractional Brownian Motion, Hawkes Processes & Point-Process Order Flow Modeling
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Proves weak functional convergence of nearly unstable heavy-tailed (power-law kernel) Hawkes order-arrival intensities to the rough Heston model via a novel C-tightness criterion for càdlàg processes.

net_new_papers.title: Microstructural Foundation for the Rough Hawkes–Heston Model
net_new_papers.authors: Yingli Wang, Yinhao Wu & Lingjiong Zhu
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Rough Volatility, Fractional Brownian Motion, Hawkes Processes & Point-Process Order Flow Modeling
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Builds a Poisson-embedded marked Hawkes order-flow model where ordinary arrivals drive rough continuous volatility and rare marked shocks generate simultaneous price jumps and volatility excitation, converging to the rough Hawkes–Heston weak solution.

net_new_papers.title: Variance-Optimal Hedging in the Rough Hawkes–Heston Model
net_new_papers.authors: Yingli Wang & Xiaoyu Wang
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Rough Volatility, Fractional Brownian Motion, Hawkes Processes & Point-Process Order Flow Modeling
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Solves the quadratic variance-optimal hedging problem in the rough Hawkes–Heston market with singular Volterra kernels and common marked jumps, proving stability of regularized finite-dimensional hedges.

net_new_papers.title: Investor Sophistication, Investor Sentiment, and Cash-Based Operating Profitability
net_new_papers.authors: Prodosh Eugene Simlai
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Cross-Sectional Corporate Cash Flow, Working Capital Efficiency, Inventory Turnover & Cash Conversion Cycle Alphas
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Demonstrates that Cash-Based Operating Profitability (CBOP) interacted with firm size yields superior abnormal returns; investor sentiment drives CBOP mispricing asymmetrically across small vs. large stocks, supporting limited-attention pricing.

net_new_papers.title: Cash Duration, Risk, and Implications for Stock Returns
net_new_papers.authors: Roi D. Taussig
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Cross-Sectional Corporate Cash Flow, Working Capital Efficiency, Inventory Turnover & Cash Conversion Cycle Alphas
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Introduces a balance-sheet "Cash Duration" measure based on corporate cash holdings; across 140,692 U.S. firm-years, higher cash duration signals higher required-return sensitivity and earns significantly higher future stock returns.

net_new_papers.title: Cash Flow Duration and Market Reactions to Earnings Announcements
net_new_papers.authors: Wenlian Gao
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Cross-Sectional Corporate Cash Flow, Working Capital Efficiency, Inventory Turnover & Cash Conversion Cycle Alphas
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Shows cash flow duration systematically shapes earnings announcement price reactions and post-announcement drift through differential sensitivity to short- vs. long-horizon cash flow news.

net_new_papers.title: GDP Growth Expectations and Cash-Flow Risk Premium
net_new_papers.authors: William N. Goetzmann, Akiko Watanabe & Masahiro Watanabe
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Cross-Sectional Corporate Cash Flow, Working Capital Efficiency, Inventory Turnover & Cash Conversion Cycle Alphas
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Measures procyclicality via cash-flow beta with respect to revisions in expected GDP growth, proving that cash-flow sensitivity to macro growth expectations commands a significant cross-sectional risk premium.

net_new_papers.title: The Working Capital Credit Multiplier
net_new_papers.authors: Heitor Almeida, Daniel Carvalho & Taehyun Kim
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Cross-Sectional Corporate Cash Flow, Working Capital Efficiency, Inventory Turnover & Cash Conversion Cycle Alphas
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Establishes a working capital credit multiplier whereby credit shocks propagate through working capital needs (inventories and receivables), amplifying real output and corporate cash flow sensitivity.

net_new_papers.title: Optimal Working Capital Management and Stock Returns
net_new_papers.authors: Tiago Coelho, Célia Oliveira & Inês Lisboa
net_new_papers.venue: *Finance a úvěr — Czech Journal of Economics and Finance*, 74(3), 292–312
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Cross-Sectional Corporate Cash Flow, Working Capital Efficiency, Inventory Turnover & Cash Conversion Cycle Alphas
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Models quadratic relationships between stock returns and CCC (plus DSO, DSI, DPO) across European listed firms, confirming a concave optimal working capital point that maximizes shareholder returns.

net_new_papers.title: From Chain to Capital: Supply Chain Risks and Working Capital Management
net_new_papers.authors: Nhan Huynh & Quynh Nga Le
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Cross-Sectional Corporate Cash Flow, Working Capital Efficiency, Inventory Turnover & Cash Conversion Cycle Alphas
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Uses text-based supply chain risk exposure on U.S. firms to show a ~6% annual increase in net working capital via higher inventories/receivables and lower payables as an operational buffer, strongest in financially constrained firms.

net_new_papers.title: Text-Based Measure of Supply Chain Risk Exposure
net_new_papers.authors: Di (Andrew) Wu
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Cross-Sectional Corporate Cash Flow, Working Capital Efficiency, Inventory Turnover & Cash Conversion Cycle Alphas
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Extracts firm-level supply chain risk exposure from earnings call Q&A using seeded word embeddings, providing an unstructured predictor of inventory buffers, working capital strain, and return risk.

net_new_papers.title: Does the Bullwhip Matter Economically? A Cross-Sectional Firm-Level Analysis
net_new_papers.authors: Opher Baron, Jeffrey L. Callen & Dan Segal
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Cross-Sectional Corporate Cash Flow, Working Capital Efficiency, Inventory Turnover & Cash Conversion Cycle Alphas
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Tests firm-level intra-firm bullwhip effect (production volatility exceeding demand volatility) in the cross-section and finds negligible negative profitability impact after endogeneity controls, reframing bullwhip as an optimal inventory response.

net_new_papers.title: The Effects of Stock-Based Incentives on Inventory Management
net_new_papers.authors: Qi Wu & Guoming Lai
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Cross-Sectional Corporate Cash Flow, Working Capital Efficiency, Inventory Turnover & Cash Conversion Cycle Alphas
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Shows executives with high stock-based incentives over-accumulate abnormal excess inventory to inflate sales or deflate COGS, creating an identifiable inventory distortion signal across U.S. retailers and manufacturers.

net_new_papers.title: The Information Content of Operational Effectiveness
net_new_papers.authors: Mary E. Barth, Jonathan Berkovitch & Doron Israeli
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Cross-Sectional Corporate Cash Flow, Working Capital Efficiency, Inventory Turnover & Cash Conversion Cycle Alphas
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Defines Operational Effectiveness (`OpEff = -CCC`) and proves higher `OpEff` predicts higher earnings announcement returns, future earnings/cash flows, and larger PEAD—especially when paired with bad earnings news that slows price discovery.

net_new_papers.title: Cash Conversion Cycle and Aggregate Stock Returns
net_new_papers.authors: Qi Lin & Xi Lin
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Cross-Sectional Corporate Cash Flow, Working Capital Efficiency, Inventory Turnover & Cash Conversion Cycle Alphas
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Aggregates bottom-up firm-level CCC (1976–2018) and shows aggregate CCC positively predicts aggregate market returns and cross-sectional size/value/momentum portfolios via cash-flow expectation errors.

net_new_papers.title: Trade Credit and Customer Portfolio Approach to Managing Cash Flow Variability
net_new_papers.authors: Nikolay Osadchiy, William Schmidt & Jing Wu
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Cross-Sectional Corporate Cash Flow, Working Capital Efficiency, Inventory Turnover & Cash Conversion Cycle Alphas
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Demonstrates that customer acquisitions lengthen DSO and CCC via lenient payment terms, whereas harmonizing trade credit terms across customers significantly reduces inbound and net cash flow volatility.

net_new_papers.title: A Tale of Two Networks: Common Ownership and Product Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.authors: Florian Ederer & Bruno Pellegrino
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: General equilibrium oligopoly model combining investor ownership-overlap networks and text-based product similarity networks; shows common ownership softens competition and increases deadweight loss ninefold (1995–2021), shifting surplus from consumers to producers.

net_new_papers.title: Common Ownership, Competition, and Corporate Governance
net_new_papers.authors: Vincenzo Denicolò & Fausto Panunzi
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Equilibrium model where investors hold competing firms to capture anticompetitive capital gains, balanced against weakened blockholder monitoring and corporate governance efficiency.

net_new_papers.title: Testing the Theory of Common Stock Ownership
net_new_papers.authors: Lysle Boller & Fiona Scott Morton
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Uses S&P 500 index additions as exogenous shocks to common ownership among product-market rivals; rivals experience significant positive abnormal returns upon entry news, consistent with higher expected industry profits.

net_new_papers.title: Common ownership, price informativeness, and corporate investment
net_new_papers.authors: In Ji Jang, Namho Kang & Ari Yezegel
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Uses financial institution mergers as shocks to common ownership; commonly held firms exhibit faster earnings news incorporation, lower noise-trade sensitivity, and higher investment-to-Tobin's Q sensitivity.

net_new_papers.title: Investor-level common ownership, stock return comovement, and competition
net_new_papers.authors: Markus Münster & Martin Walther
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Using S&P 500 holdings, shows higher investor-level common ownership predicts stronger pairwise stock return correlations, driven primarily by long-term investors and reduced product-market competition.

net_new_papers.title: Does common ownership constrain managerial rent extraction? Evidence from insider trading profitability
net_new_papers.authors: Shenglan Chen, Hui Ma, Qiang Wu & Hao Zhang
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Shows common institutional ownership curtails corporate insider trading profitability via cross-firm benchmarking and governance monitoring, reducing information asymmetry alpha for insiders.

net_new_papers.title: Common institutional ownership and commonality in liquidity
net_new_papers.authors: *Accounting & Finance*
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Finds common institutional ownership reduces cross-stock commonality in liquidity through synergistic governance and enhanced information transparency, though attenuated by exit threats.

net_new_papers.title: Does common institutional ownership affect systemic risk of non-financial firms?
net_new_papers.authors: Xiao-Lin Li, Jiawei Hao & Liang Liu
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Shows common institutional ownership (CIO) amplifies non-financial firms' systemic risk by propagating idiosyncratic tail risk across CIO-linked networks and increasing risk interconnectedness, especially in illiquid firms.

net_new_papers.title: Does common institutional ownership matter for equity mispricing?
net_new_papers.authors: *Finance Research Letters*
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Documents that common institutional ownership mitigates cross-sectional equity mispricing by reducing information asymmetry, most strongly in competitive, non-monopolistic industries.

net_new_papers.title: The Present Value of Future Market Power
net_new_papers.authors: Thummim Cho, Marco Grotteria, Lukas Kremens & Howard Kung
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Derives a present-value identity linking equity prices to expected future markups; expected markups explain half of U.S. valuation growth since 1980, correlate negatively with discount rates over time, and positively predict cross-sectional abnormal returns.

net_new_papers.title: Product Market Competition, Labor Mobility, and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
net_new_papers.authors: Shamim Ahmed, Ziwen Bu, Xiaoxia Ye & Hui Chen
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Production-based asset pricing model proving that lower systematic risk exposure in concentrated industries dampens operating leverage; labor mobility positively predicts cross-sectional stock returns exclusively in competitive industries.

net_new_papers.title: Product market competition and stock return dependence
net_new_papers.authors: *Finance Research Letters*
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Spatial econometric model of daily idiosyncratic stock returns among product-market rivals; contagion dominates competitive substitution, with stronger asymmetric spillovers from negative rival shocks in fluid, low-concentration markets.

net_new_papers.title: Advertising, product market competition and stock returns
net_new_papers.authors: *Review of Quantitative Finance and Accounting*
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Across U.S. equities (1977–2018), past advertising intensity negatively predicts future stock returns only in competitive industries, while competitive-industry stocks earn higher expected returns than concentrated-industry peers.

net_new_papers.title: How does competition affect retail banking? Quasi-experimental evidence
net_new_papers.authors: *Journal of Financial Economics*
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Uses quasi-experimental shocks to local banking competition to quantify how market concentration and antitrust-relevant rivalry shape deposit spreads, lending markups, and financial intermediary profitability.

net_new_papers.title: Mergers and market power: Evidence from rivals' responses
net_new_papers.authors: *DICE Discussion Paper 323*
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Uses European Commission antitrust market definitions to identify exact product-market rivals; rivals significantly raise markups and profits post-merger while cutting output and employment, especially in concentrated markets.

net_new_papers.title: Product market competition and the value of corporate cash
net_new_papers.authors: *International Review of Financial Analysis*
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Uses IPO suspensions as exogenous shocks lowering product-market competition; reduced rivalry decreases the marginal market value of corporate cash reserves via an agency slack channel.

net_new_papers.title: Modelling fire sale contagion across banks and non-banks
net_new_papers.authors: Fabio Caccioli, Gerardo Ferrara & Amanah Ramadiah
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Multi-layer overlapping-portfolio network model uniting banks and non-bank financial intermediaries; quantifies cross-sector fire-sale price impact and systemic capital depletion under correlated liquidation shocks.

net_new_papers.title: Preventing Price-Mediated Contagion Due to Fire Sales Externalities: Strategic Foundations of Macroprudential Regulation
net_new_papers.authors: Yann Braouezec & Keyvan Kiani
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Game-theoretic financial network model of strategic fire-sale externalities; derives endogenous liquidation cascades and optimal macroprudential leverage caps to eliminate price-mediated contagion equilibria.

net_new_papers.title: ETFs and tail dependence: Evidence from Chinese stock market
net_new_papers.authors: Wei Ning, Jiahua Zhao & Fuwei Jiang
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Shows ETF ownership similarity creates a non-fundamental tail-dependence network among constituent stocks via discount arbitrage, propagating idiosyncratic tail shocks across basket peers.

net_new_papers.title: ETF ownership and stock pricing efficiency: The role of ETF arbitrage
net_new_papers.authors: Guanhua Chen, Xiangli Liu, Xiao Liu & Zhihua Zhao
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Financial Networks, Systemic Interconnectedness, Common Ownership & Antitrust / Product-Market Rivalry
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Constructs daily ETF holding networks from intraday PCF data; higher ETF ownership intensifies ETF arbitrage and noise contagion from ETFs to underlying equities, degrading cross-sectional pricing efficiency.

net_new_papers.title: Global systemic risk dynamic network connectedness during the COVID-19 pandemic

net_new_papers.track: Track 23: Mergers, Acquisitions & Antitrust Intervention: Regulatory Deal-Spread Risk & Peer Rivalry Spillovers
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Uncovers a "revaluation spread" where industry peers experience positive CARs around public-target deals but negative CARs around private-target deals, predicting subsequent industry-level stock returns.

net_new_papers.title: Government intervention in European mergers and acquisitions
net_new_papers.authors: Nuria Alcalde & Ronan Powell
net_new_papers.venue: North American Journal of Economics and Finance
net_new_papers.track: Track 23: Mergers, Acquisitions & Antitrust Intervention: Regulatory Deal-Spread Risk & Peer Rivalry Spillovers
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Analyzes 1,574 EU rival firms around cross-border M&A interventions, finding rivals of intervened targets earn significantly lower announcement returns as investors price expected regulatory blocks.

net_new_papers.title: The Effects of Horizontal Merger Operating Efficiencies on Rivals, Customers, and Suppliers
net_new_papers.authors: Gennaro Bernile & Evgeny Lyandres
net_new_papers.track: Track 23: Mergers, Acquisitions & Antitrust Intervention: Regulatory Deal-Spread Risk & Peer Rivalry Spillovers
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Separates cost-savings vs. productivity-gain merger synergies, showing horizontal merger announcements generate distinct cross-sectional return spillovers across TNIC rivals, customers, and suppliers.

net_new_papers.title: Antitrust merger review costs and acquirer lobbying
net_new_papers.authors: Jana P. Fidrmuc, Peter Roosenboom & Eden Quxian Zhang
net_new_papers.track: Track 23: Mergers, Acquisitions & Antitrust Intervention: Regulatory Deal-Spread Risk & Peer Rivalry Spillovers
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Quantifies an average -2.8% acquirer value loss on adverse antitrust review outcomes and shows pre-announcement lobbying improves regulatory clearance odds in horizontal deals.

net_new_papers.title: Merger Options and Risk Arbitrage
net_new_papers.authors: Peter Van Tassel
net_new_papers.track: Track 23: Mergers, Acquisitions & Antitrust Intervention: Regulatory Deal-Spread Risk & Peer Rivalry Spillovers
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Develops a dynamic asset pricing model combining target stock and option prices to extract risk-neutral deal-completion probabilities and forecast merger-arbitrage Sharpe ratios and crash risk.

net_new_papers.title: No News Is News: Do Markets Underreact to Nothing?
net_new_papers.authors: Stefano Giglio & Kelly Shue
net_new_papers.venue: The Review of Financial Studies / NBER WP 18914
net_new_papers.track: Track 23: Mergers, Acquisitions & Antitrust Intervention: Regulatory Deal-Spread Risk & Peer Rivalry Spillovers
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Estimates hump-shaped merger completion hazard rates over event time, proving markets underreact to the passage of time without regulatory/deal news and generating predictable merger-arbitrage returns.

net_new_papers.title: The surprising power of the pre-IPO grey market to mitigate information asymmetry and winner's curse for retail investors
net_new_papers.authors: Sachin Mathur, Mayank Joshipura, Raman Kumar
net_new_papers.venue: *The Quarterly Review of Economics and Finance*, 109(C)
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: IPO Underpricing, SPAC Redemption Arbitrage, Lockup Expirations & Seasoned Equity Offerings (SEOs)
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Shows pre-IPO grey market premia (GMP) anticipate institutional bookbuilding bids and generate positive allotment-weighted returns that persist for 12 months without sentiment reversal.

net_new_papers.title: De-SPAC performance under better aligned sponsor contracts
net_new_papers.authors: Yao-Min Chiang, Woojin Kim, Bokyung Park, Tae Jun Yoon
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: IPO Underpricing, SPAC Redemption Arbitrage, Lockup Expirations & Seasoned Equity Offerings (SEOs)
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Contrasts Korean SPACs with U.S. SPACs, showing that tighter sponsor contract alignment eliminates post-merger underperformance and yields positive/non-negative de-SPAC buy-and-hold abnormal returns.

net_new_papers.title: Retail Investors and the Going Public Decision: SPACs vs. IPOs
net_new_papers.authors: Debarshi K. Nandy, Yaxuan Wen
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: IPO Underpricing, SPAC Redemption Arbitrage, Lockup Expirations & Seasoned Equity Offerings (SEOs)
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Documents retail order flow around SPACs (weak pre-announcement, surging post-target announcement due to the $10 redemption floor) and compares post-listing retail trading across de-SPACs vs. IPOs.

net_new_papers.title: Pre-IPO dividend and post-IPO stock price crash risk
net_new_papers.authors: Jing Zhang, Xiaoyue Li, Yong Zhao, Jinyu Feng
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: IPO Underpricing, SPAC Redemption Arbitrage, Lockup Expirations & Seasoned Equity Offerings (SEOs)
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Identifies a U-shaped relationship between pre-IPO cash dividend payouts to insiders and post-IPO crash risk, especially under IPO pricing caps and pre-IPO underinvestment.

net_new_papers.title: Information production in start-up firms: SPACs vs. Traditional IPOs
net_new_papers.authors: Keiichi Hori, Hiroshi Osano
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: IPO Underpricing, SPAC Redemption Arbitrage, Lockup Expirations & Seasoned Equity Offerings (SEOs)
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Compares equilibrium information production in SPACs vs. traditional IPOs, showing traditional IPOs are more informationally efficient unless IPO timelines/costs are excessive or average firm quality declines.

net_new_papers.title: Sponsor reputation and agency conflicts in SPACs
net_new_papers.authors: Alfonso Del Giudice, Andrea Signori
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: IPO Underpricing, SPAC Redemption Arbitrage, Lockup Expirations & Seasoned Equity Offerings (SEOs)
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Distinguishes repeat PE-backed SPAC sponsors (lower merger completion, significantly higher post-merger returns) from one-off executive sponsors who extract lucrative terms at investors' expense.

net_new_papers.title: Impact of post-IPO investments on the long-term financial market performance of Japanese IPOs: A preregistered report
net_new_papers.authors: Colette Southam, Guoliang (Frank) Jiang, James Todd, Isaac Tonkin
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: IPO Underpricing, SPAC Redemption Arbitrage, Lockup Expirations & Seasoned Equity Offerings (SEOs)
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Tests the "new issues puzzle" via actual post-IPO use-of-proceeds allocation (debt repayment, CapEx, working capital, M&A) to explain 3- to 5-year post-IPO return drift.

net_new_papers.title: SPACs
net_new_papers.authors: Minmo Gahng, Jay R. Ritter, Donghang Zhang
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: IPO Underpricing, SPAC Redemption Arbitrage, Lockup Expirations & Seasoned Equity Offerings (SEOs)
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Benchmarks SPAC IPO unit/redemption arbitrage returns (high annualized riskless-floor returns for SPAC IPO investors and sponsors) against deeply negative equally weighted post-merger de-SPAC returns.

net_new_papers.title: A Sober Look at SPACs
net_new_papers.authors: Michael Klausner, Michael Ohlrogge, Emily Ruan
net_new_papers.venue: *ECGI Finance Working Paper* 746/2021 (*Yale Journal on Regulation*)
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: IPO Underpricing, SPAC Redemption Arbitrage, Lockup Expirations & Seasoned Equity Offerings (SEOs)
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Decomposes SPAC dilution (sponsor promote, warrants, underwriting fees on redeemed shares), showing $10.00 IPO proceeds shrink to $4.10–$5.70 net cash per share at merger and drive steep post-merger losses.

net_new_papers.title: SPACs and the regulation gap: The effect of first SEC intervention on share and warrant returns
net_new_papers.authors: Evrim Akdoğu, Şerif Aziz Şimşir, Merve Meriç Yılmaz
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: IPO Underpricing, SPAC Redemption Arbitrage, Lockup Expirations & Seasoned Equity Offerings (SEOs)
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Analyzes share and warrant abnormal returns around SEC warrant-accounting intervention, showing SPAC warrant structures drive announcement-return cross-sectional dispersion.

net_new_papers.title: Textual Information and IPO Underpricing: A Machine Learning Approach
net_new_papers.authors: Apostolos G. Katsafados, Ion Androutsopoulos, Ilias Chalkidis, Manos Fergadiotis, George N. Leledakis, Emmanouil G. Pyrgiotakis
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: IPO Underpricing, SPAC Redemption Arbitrage, Lockup Expirations & Seasoned Equity Offerings (SEOs)
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Trains ML classifiers on 2,481 U.S. IPO S-1 filings (1997–2016), showing prospectus textual features substantially improve out-of-sample IPO underpricing prediction over financial ratios alone.

net_new_papers.title: Informed short selling around SEO announcements
net_new_papers.authors: Sanjay Deshmukh, Keith Jacks Gamble, Keith M. Howe
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: IPO Underpricing, SPAC Redemption Arbitrage, Lockup Expirations & Seasoned Equity Offerings (SEOs)
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Documents informed short selling ahead of SEO announcements: spikes in pre-announcement short interest predict more negative announcement returns and inferior long-run post-SEO performance, especially in shelf offers.

net_new_papers.title: Changing the rules again: Short selling in connection with public equity offers
net_new_papers.authors: Don M. Autore, Dominique Gehy
net_new_papers.track: Track 24: IPO Underpricing, SPAC Redemption Arbitrage, Lockup Expirations & Seasoned Equity Offerings (SEOs)
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Evaluates SEC Rule 105 (5-day pre-offer shorting ban), finding it unintentionally widens SEO discounts on overnight offers by excluding short-selling buyers from the offering syndicate.

net_new_papers.title: The cross-section of expected stock returns in the property/liability insurance industry
net_new_papers.authors: Semir Ben Ammar, Martin Eling, Andreas Milidonis
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Insurance & Reinsurance Finance: Catastrophe Bonds (CAT/ILS), Underwriting Cycles & Insurer Asset-Side Risk-Taking
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Shows standard Fama-French factors fail to price P&C insurer equities and introduces an insurance-specific five-factor model (INS5) capturing sector-to-market spreads and underwriting risk.

net_new_papers.title: Asset pricing and extreme event risk: Common factors in ILS fund returns
net_new_papers.authors: Alexander Braun, Semir Ben Ammar, Martin Eling
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Insurance & Reinsurance Finance: Catastrophe Bonds (CAT/ILS), Underwriting Cycles & Insurer Asset-Side Risk-Taking
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Extracts common risk factors driving Insurance-Linked Securities (ILS) fund returns, quantifying catastrophe tail-risk premia and diversification properties relative to traditional asset classes.

net_new_papers.title: New Perspectives on Insurance
net_new_papers.authors: Ralph S. J. Koijen, Motohiro Yogo
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Insurance & Reinsurance Finance: Catastrophe Bonds (CAT/ILS), Underwriting Cycles & Insurer Asset-Side Risk-Taking
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Synthesizes modern financial-intermediation models of insurance, linking regulatory frictions, asset-side reaching for yield, liability guarantees, and reinsurance capital supply.

net_new_papers.title: Cyber insurance-linked securities
net_new_papers.authors: Alexander Braun, Martin Eling, Christoph Jaenicke
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Insurance & Reinsurance Finance: Catastrophe Bonds (CAT/ILS), Underwriting Cycles & Insurer Asset-Side Risk-Taking
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Evaluates supply-demand equilibrium for cyber ILS by comparing insurer cost of equity against investor-required Rates on Line, identifying cyber-risk modeling gaps that govern market viability.

net_new_papers.title: Pricing extreme mortality risk in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic
net_new_papers.authors: Han Li, Haibo Liu, Qihe Tang, Zhongyi Yuan
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Insurance & Reinsurance Finance: Catastrophe Bonds (CAT/ILS), Underwriting Cycles & Insurer Asset-Side Risk-Taking
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Models joint interest-rate and excess-mortality dynamics via a bivariate affine jump-diffusion with correlated diffusions and co-jumps, solving for mortality-bond diffusion and jump risk premia.

net_new_papers.title: The ILS loss experience: natural catastrophe issues 2001–2020
net_new_papers.authors: Morton Lane
net_new_papers.venue: *The Geneva Papers on Risk and Insurance*, Vol. 49(1), 97–137
net_new_papers.track: Track 25: Insurance & Reinsurance Finance: Catastrophe Bonds (CAT/ILS), Underwriting Cycles & Insurer Asset-Side Risk-Taking
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Audits two decades of natural-catastrophe ILS loss distributions, trigger mechanics, and realized vs. modeled expected losses across primary and aggregate CAT bond structures.

net_new_papers.title: Unconventional Monetary Policy and Deposit Retention
net_new_papers.authors: Philip Strahan & Tuo Yang

net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Proves that prolonged ZLB and QE shifted bank deposit composition toward rate-sensitive, large depositors; once monetary policy normalized, both deposit flow sensitivity and deposit betas surged with prior QE/ZLB exposure.

net_new_papers.title: Deposit Betas: Up, Up, and Away?
net_new_papers.authors: Alena Kang-Landsberg, Stephan Luck & Matthew Plosser
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Banking Microstructure: Deposit Betas, Uninsured Deposit Runs, Unrealized HTM Losses & Wholesale Funding Fragility
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Documents rising pass-through of the federal funds rate to deposit rates across deposit categories through 2022:Q4, showing banks substitute out of regular deposits into high-beta time deposits and Federal Home Loan Bank (FHLB) advances.

net_new_papers.title: Interest rate and run risks in euro area banks during the 2022–2023 monetary cycle
net_new_papers.authors: Jonathan Rice & Giulia Maria Guerrini
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Banking Microstructure: Deposit Betas, Uninsured Deposit Runs, Unrealized HTM Losses & Wholesale Funding Fragility
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Estimates economic net worth for 139 euro area banks; finds unrealized bond/loan losses averaged ~30% of equity (half offset by deposit franchise and swaps) and banks with larger unrealized losses raised deposit rates by less.

net_new_papers.title: Monetary Tightening and U.S. Bank Fragility in 2023: Mark-to-Market Losses and Uninsured Depositor Runs?
net_new_papers.authors: Erica Xuewei Jiang, Gregor Matvos, Tomasz Piskorski & Amit Seru
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Banking Microstructure: Deposit Betas, Uninsured Deposit Runs, Unrealized HTM Losses & Wholesale Funding Fragility

net_new_papers.title: The 2023 Banking Turmoil and the Bank Term Funding Program
net_new_papers.authors: David P. Glancy, Felicia Ionescu, Elizabeth C. Klee, Antonis Kotidis, Michael Siemer & Andrei Zlate
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Banking Microstructure: Deposit Betas, Uninsured Deposit Runs, Unrealized HTM Losses & Wholesale Funding Fragility

net_new_papers.title: Who Can Tell Which Banks Will Fail?
net_new_papers.authors: Kristian Blickle, Markus Brunnermeier & Stephan Luck

net_new_papers.title: Failing Banks

net_new_papers.title: Bank Fragility and Reclassification of Securities into HTM

net_new_papers.title: A Tale of Two Runs: Depositor Responses to Bank Solvency Risk

net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Compares depositor run behavior across shocks using account-level data, showing uninsured depositors and those with shorter bank relationships withdraw sharply in response to solvency risk signals.

net_new_papers.title: The dark side of bank wholesale funding

net_new_papers.authors: Dong Beom Choi & Hyun-Soo Choi

net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Shows that monetary tightening induces retail deposit outflows, forcing banks—especially smaller ones—to substitute toward runnable wholesale funding, thereby increasing balance-sheet fragility and amplifying monetary transmission.

net_new_papers.title: Double bank runs and liquidity risk management
net_new_papers.authors: Filippo Ippolito, José-Luis Peydró, Andrea Polo & Enrico Sette
net_new_papers.track: Track 26: Banking Microstructure: Deposit Betas, Uninsured Deposit Runs, Unrealized HTM Losses & Wholesale Funding Fragility
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Demonstrates that banks heavily exposed to interbank wholesale funding simultaneously faced corporate credit-line drawdowns ("double runs") during the 2007–2008 freeze, curtailing credit supply unless pre-hedged with liquid buffers.

net_new_papers.title: Bank Funding Risk, Reference Rates, and Credit Supply
net_new_papers.authors: Harry Cooperman, Darrell Duffie, Stephan Luck, Zachry Wang & Yilin (David) Yang

net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Shows that corporate credit-line drawdowns covary positively with bank wholesale funding stress, creating debt-overhang costs for bank equity holders that dampen credit supply—exacerbated by transitioning from credit-sensitive LIBOR to risk-free SOFR.

net_new_papers.title: Fragile wholesale deposits, liquidity risk, and banks' maturity transformation
net_new_papers.authors: Carola Müller, Matias Ossandon Busch, Miguel Sarmiento & Freddy Pinzon-Puerto

net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Documents structural shifts in U.S. Treasury auction bidding participation (investment funds vs. primary dealers), showing how bidder composition alters auction tails and secondary-market price discovery.

net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Synthesizes sovereign repo market mechanics across collateral reuse, haircuts, and central clearing, showing how short-term funding links dealer balance sheets, MMFs, and hedge fund basis leverage.

net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Decomposes the on-the-run/off-the-run Treasury price spread into expected future repo specialness dividends and a priced special-collateral risk premium using affine term-structure regressions.

net_new_papers.title: Bond market intermediation and the Role of Repo
net_new_papers.authors: Yesol Huh, Sebastian Infante

net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Models how dealers use special repo and collateral rehypothecation to intermediate cash Treasury order flow, linking repo specialness spikes directly to secondary-market bid-ask spreads.

net_new_papers.title: Haircut, Interest Rate, and Collateral Quality in the Tri-Party Repo Market: Evidence and Theory
net_new_papers.authors: Sangyup Choi, Inkee Jang, Kee-Youn Kang, Hyunpyung Kim
net_new_papers.track: Track 27: Treasury Auctions, Repo Specialness, Tri-Party Haircuts, Quarter-End SLR Window Dressing & Treasury Cash-Futures Basis
net_new_papers.key_mechanism: Analyzes transaction-level tri-party repo contracts, characterizing the joint equilibrium determination of haircuts, repo rates, and collateral quality across dealer-lender pairs.

net_new_papers.title: Treasury Tri-party Repo Pricing
net_new_papers.authors: Mark Paddrik, Carlos Ramirez
